entries.original:
A sphere-valued map cannot vanish outside a compact set. As approved by
the user on 2026-10-23, interpret spatial compact support as compact support
of a perturbation from a **fixed unit vector**, locally uniformly in time.
This is a disclosed nontrivial interpretation, not a claimed author-issued
correction.

Let \(n,m\geq1\) be integers and let
\(u:\mathbb R^n\times(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^m\) be jointly smooth.
Fix \(q\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(|q|=1\). Assume:

1. \(|u(x,t)|=1\) for all \(x\) and \(t>0\).
2. The acceleration \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu\) is normal to the sphere at
   \(u\): at each point there is a real scalar \(a(x,t)\) with
   \(u_{tt}-\Delta_xu=a u\). No regularity of the selected scalar is
   assumed.
3. For every \(0<s<t<\infty\), a compact set
   \(C_{[s,t]}\subset\mathbb R^n\) exists such that \(u(x,r)=q\) for
   \(x\notin C_{[s,t]}\), \(r\in[s,t]\).

With Euclidean norms and Lebesgue measure, define

\[
e(x,t)=|u_t(x,t)|^2+\sum_{j=1}^n|\partial_{x_j}u(x,t)|^2,
\qquad E(t)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e(x,t)\,dx.
\]

The spatial gradient square is the Frobenius square, and
\(\Delta_xu=\sum_j\partial_{x_jx_j}u\) component by component.
Prove integrability of \(e(\cdot,t)\), differentiability of \(E\),
and \(E'(t)=0\) for every \(t>0\). No assertion at time zero is required.

entries.correspondence: The parameters n,m are naturals constrained by H001 to be ≥1; X and V are the original Euclidean spaces, Fin n indexes the n coordinate directions, and volume is Euclidean Lebesgue measure. U is an arbitrary total representative on X×ℝ, required C∞ only on the open positive-time domain; restriction gives exactly a jointly smooth source u. Conversely each source u has a total zero extension, smooth on that open domain, so no hypothesis about time ≤0 is introduced. Locality of Fréchet derivatives on an open neighborhood and the checked affine-section bridge T003 identify every directional field with the original ordinary partial derivative, in both directions; changing the extension changes no positive-time derivative. H001 retains the fixed unit q, H002 retains the unit constraint and a fresh existential real scalar at each point without regularity, and H003 retains one common compact spatial set for each closed positive-time slab and the same q for all points/times. density is exactly the sum of the time square and all spatial squares with coefficient 1, lap is the componentwise sum, and energy is its Lebesgue integral. The terminal quantifies every positive real t and asserts integrability, ordinary differentiability and zero ordinary derivative. Integrability makes the total Bochner integral the actual finite energy; this conjunction is exactly the requested target in both directions. No statement at zero or scalar-field selection is asserted.
